```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# ---- Repository root (portable) ---------------------------------------------
# Walk up from this file to the folder holding scripts/00_run_all.R. Set the
# RHD_REPO_ROOT environment variable when rendering a copy outside the repo.
find_repo_root <- function() {
  env <- Sys.getenv("RHD_REPO_ROOT")
  if (nzchar(env)) return(normalizePath(env, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE))
  d <- tryCatch(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), error = function(e) getwd())
  d <- normalizePath(d, winslash = "/", mustWork = FALSE)
  repeat {
    if (file.exists(file.path(d, "scripts", "00_run_all.R")) &&
        file.exists(file.path(d, "R", "abcd_engine.R"))) return(d)
    up <- dirname(d)
    if (identical(up, d))
      stop("Cannot find the repository root (folder holding scripts/00_run_all.R). ",
           "Set RHD_REPO_ROOT.", call. = FALSE)
    d <- up
  }
}
ROOT      <- find_repo_root()
COUNTRIES <- c("Indonesia", "Uganda")

# ---- Saved artifacts only: the deck never runs or modifies the pipeline -------
artifact <- function(script, ...) {
  p <- file.path(ROOT, ...)
  if (!file.exists(p))
    stop("Missing pipeline artifact: ", p, "\n  Produced by scripts/", script,
         " (run scripts/00_run_all.R with the matching COUNTRY). ",
         "The deck reads saved results only and never re-runs the model.", call. = FALSE)
  p
}
load_country <- function(ct) list(
  out  = readRDS(artifact("06_run_prevention_model.R", "output", ct, "out_model", paste0(ct, ".rds"))),
  econ = readRDS(artifact("08_economic_evaluation.R", "output", ct, "tables", "rhd_economic_results.rds")),
  bs   = readRDS(artifact("05_build_baseline.R", "data", ct, "baseline_state.rds")),
  cal  = readRDS(artifact("04_calibration_random_tp.R and 04b_calibrate_structural.R",
                          "data", ct, "calibrated_rhd_parameters.rds")),
  gbd  = as.data.table(readRDS(artifact("01_prepare_inputs.R", "data", ct, "temp_baseline_rates_gbd.rds"))),
  pop  = as.data.table(readRDS(artifact("02_build_demography.R", "data", ct, "pop_observed.rds"))))
D <- setNames(lapply(COUNTRIES, load_country), COUNTRIES)

# Input-integrity checks stop the render with the files involved and the upstream
# fix. They test consistency of the saved artifacts, never an expected result.
check <- function(ok, msg, fix = "re-run scripts/00_run_all.R for that COUNTRY")
  if (!isTRUE(ok)) stop("Deck input check failed: ", msg, "\n  Upstream regeneration needed: ", fix, call. = FALSE)

# ---- Formatting (strings are valid in markdown and in LaTeX table cells) ------
fmt_n   <- function(x, d = 0) formatC(round(x, d), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
fmt_h   <- function(x) fmt_n(round(x, -2))                       # nearest hundred
fmt_pct <- function(x, d = 0) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = d), "\\%")
fmt_cov <- function(x) paste0(formatC(100 * x, format = "f", digits = 2, drop0trailing = TRUE), "\\%")
fmt_usd <- function(x, d = 0) paste0("US\\$", fmt_n(x, d))
fmt_bn  <- function(x, d = 2) paste0("US\\$", formatC(x / 1e9, format = "f", digits = d), " bn")
fmt_mn  <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(x / 1e6, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","), " m")
fmt_x   <- function(x, d = 1) paste0(formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d), "$\\times$")
fmt_f   <- function(x, d = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d)
fmt_e   <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 1)
# A ratio to one in words ("15\% below", "8\% above", "within 1\% of").
rel_phrase <- function(r, tol = 0.01) {
  if (length(r) != 1 || !is.finite(r)) return("not comparable with")
  if (abs(r - 1) < tol) return(paste0("within ", fmt_pct(tol), " of"))
  paste0(fmt_pct(abs(r - 1)), if (r < 1) " below" else " above")
}
# Scale-up relative to reference ("63\% smaller", "essentially unchanged").
chg_phrase <- function(new, old, up = "larger", down = "smaller", d = 0, tol = 5e-5) {
  if (length(old) != 1 || !is.finite(old) || old == 0) return("not defined")
  r <- new / old - 1
  if (abs(r) < tol) return("essentially unchanged")
  paste(fmt_pct(abs(r), d), if (r < 0) down else up)
}
grp_lo <- setNames(c(0, 1, 2, 5, seq(10, 95, by = 5)),
                   c("<1 year", "12-23 months", "2-4 years", "5-9 years", paste0(seq(10, 90, by = 5), "-", seq(14, 94, by = 5), " years"), "95+ years"))
age_to_grp <- function(a) names(grp_lo)[findInterval(a, grp_lo)]

# ---- Integrity checks: country, scenarios, years, specification, units, pairing ---
for (ct in COUNTRIES) {
  d  <- D[[ct]]
  w  <- as.data.table(d$out$wsd); s <- as.data.table(d$out$stages)
  yy <- as.integer(d$out$meta$years); sc <- d$cal$stage_calibration; bp <- sc$best_parameters
  st <- d$bs$states[[1]]
  fx <- paste("re-run 05 -> 08 for", ct)
  check(identical(unique(as.character(w$location)), ct), paste(ct, "model output holds another location"))
  check(identical(unique(as.character(s$location)), ct), paste(ct, "stage table holds another location"))
  check(identical(d$bs$locations, ct) && identical(d$cal$meta$location, ct),
        paste(ct, "baseline/calibration bundle holds another location"))
  check(unique(d$gbd$location_name) == ct, paste(ct, "GBD extract holds another location"))
  check(!grepl("^FAILED", as.character(sc$status)) && !is.null(bp),
        paste(ct, "Layer-2 calibration status is", sc$status), paste("fix and re-run 04b -> 08 for", ct))
  check(setequal(unique(w$scenario), c("ref", "sap")) && setequal(unique(s$scenario), c("ref", "sap")),
        paste(ct, "scenarios are not exactly ref + sap"))
  check(identical(sort(unique(as.integer(w$year))), yy) &&
        identical(as.integer(d$bs$meta$years), yy) &&
        identical(sort(as.integer(d$econ$incremental$year)), yy),
        paste(ct, "analysis years differ across model, baseline and economics"), fx)
  spec <- c(sc$spec$mortality_structure, sc$spec$sap_mechanism)
  check(identical(spec, c(d$bs$meta$mortality_structure, d$bs$meta$sap_mechanism)) &&
          identical(spec, c(d$out$meta$mortality_structure, d$out$meta$sap_mechanism)),
        paste(ct, "mortality structure / SAP mechanism differ between calibration, baseline and model"), fx)
  check(isTRUE(all.equal(unlist(st$transitions), unlist(bp$transitions))) && isTRUE(all.equal(st$p_rhd_death, bp$p_rhd_death)),
        paste(ct, "baseline stage parameters differ from the calibrated best parameters"), fx)
  if (!is.null(bp$initial_state))
    check(all(vapply(c("A", "B", "C", "D"), function(k) isTRUE(all.equal(unname(st$seed[[k]]), unname(bp$initial_state[[k]]))), NA)),
          paste(ct, "the model seed differs from the calibrated analysis-start state"), fx)
  rc <- bp$reference_care_in_calibration
  check(abs(rc$treatment_effective - st$coverage$ref$eff_treatment[1]) < 1e-9 && abs(rc$surgery - st$coverage$ref$surgery[1]) < 1e-9 &&
          abs(rc$adherence - st$coverage$ref$adherence[1]) < 1e-9,
        paste(ct, "reference care in the calibration differs from the reference arm"), paste("re-run 04b -> 08 for", ct))
  check(all(is.finite(as.matrix(w[, .(well, sick, newcases, dead, pop, all.mx)]))),
        paste(ct, "non-finite values in the aggregate model table"))
  pp <- dcast(w[, .(pop = sum(pop)), by = .(scenario, year)], year ~ scenario, value.var = "pop")
  check(max(abs(pp$ref - pp$sap)) < 1e-6, paste(ct, "arms do not share one population"))
  check(nrow(d$econ$summary[location == ct]) == 1, paste(ct, "economic summary row missing"))
  ab <- merge(s[, .(stg = A + B + C + D), by = .(scenario, year, sex, age)],
              w[, .(scenario, year, sex, age, sick)], by = c("scenario", "year", "sex", "age"))
  check(nrow(ab) == nrow(w) && max(abs(ab$stg - ab$sick)) < 1e-6,
        paste(ct, "stages A-D do not sum to the aggregate RHD stock"))
  if (identical(sc$spec$mortality_structure, "D_only"))
    check(s[, all(rhd_deaths_A == 0 & rhd_deaths_B == 0 & rhd_deaths_C == 0)], paste(ct, "D-only run has deaths outside stage D"), fx)
  if (identical(sc$spec$sap_mechanism, "progression")) {
    ef <- st$effects
    check(s[, max(abs(eff_cf - 1))] < 1e-12 &&
            s[, max(abs(sap_prog_mult_A_to_B - (1 - sap_effective_protection * (1 - ef$sap_hr_A_to_B))),
                    abs(sap_prog_mult_C_to_D - (1 - sap_effective_protection * (1 - ef$sap_hr_C_to_D))))] < 1e-9,
          paste(ct, "progression-mode SAP trace does not match the saved hazard ratios"), fx)
  }
  dd <- dcast(w[, .(d = sum(dead)), by = .(scenario, year)], year ~ scenario, value.var = "d")
  ee <- merge(dd, as.data.table(d$econ$incremental)[, .(year, deaths_avert)], by = "year")
  check(nrow(ee) == length(yy) && max(abs(ee$ref - ee$sap - ee$deaths_avert)) < 1e-6,
        paste(ct, "economic deaths averted were not computed from this model run"), paste("re-run 08 for", ct))
  # screening encounters follow the saved schedule; economics use the GNI-anchored,
  # VSL-only valuation (outputs from before that revision stop the render here)
  enc <- st$coverage$screen_encounters_per_person
  check(!is.null(enc) && !is.null(st$coverage$screen_schedule) && !is.null(d$out$diag$screening_by_year),
        paste(ct, "baseline / model output predate the screening-encounter revision"), paste("re-run 03 -> 08 for", ct))
  check(s[, .(e = sum(n_screened), c = screen_coverage[1], w = sum(pop * enc[as.character(age)])), by = .(scenario, year)][
          , max(abs(e - c * w) / pmax(e, 1))] < 1e-9,
        paste(ct, "screening encounters differ from reach x schedule x population"), fx)
  inc_ct <- as.data.table(d$econ$incremental); ep_ct <- d$econ$params
  check(!is.null(ep_ct$gni_pc_base) && all(inc_ct$benefit_gdp == 0) && isTRUE(all.equal(inc_ct$benefit_total, inc_ct$benefit_vsl)),
        paste(ct, "economics predate the GNI-anchored, VSL-only valuation"), paste("re-run 08 for", ct))
}
check(identical(D$Indonesia$out$meta$years, D$Uganda$out$meta$years),
      "Indonesia and Uganda runs cover different analysis years")
check(D$Indonesia$econ$discount_base_year == D$Uganda$econ$discount_base_year,
      "countries use different discount base years")
check(identical(D$Indonesia$cal$stage_calibration$spec[c("mortality_structure", "sap_mechanism")],
                D$Uganda$cal$stage_calibration$spec[c("mortality_structure", "sap_mechanism")]),
      "the countries were calibrated under different specifications; the deck compares them under one",
      "re-run both countries under one mortality structure and SAP mechanism")
SPEC   <- D$Indonesia$cal$stage_calibration$spec
D_ONLY <- identical(SPEC$mortality_structure, "D_only")
PROG   <- identical(SPEC$sap_mechanism, "progression")

# ---- Per-country results computed from the saved objects ---------------------
summarise_country <- function(ct) {
  d  <- D[[ct]]; meta <- d$out$meta
  w  <- as.data.table(d$out$wsd); s <- as.data.table(d$out$stages)
  ep <- d$econ$params; dby <- d$econ$discount_base_year
  yy <- as.integer(meta$years); y0 <- min(yy); y1 <- max(yy); ye <- as.integer(meta$ramp_end)
  cal <- d$cal; sc <- cal$stage_calibration; oc <- sc$objective_components; bp <- sc$best_parameters
  eda <- sc$excess_death_attribution
  prev_obs <- if (!is.null(sc$spec$prev_obs)) sc$spec$prev_obs else oc$prev_obs_convention
  w <- merge(w, s[, .(scenario, age, sex, year, living_rhd_start)], by = c("scenario", "age", "sex", "year"))
  w[, prev_obs := switch(prev_obs, start = living_rhd_start, end = sick, mid = 0.5 * (living_rhd_start + sick))]
  agg  <- w[, .(pop = sum(pop), inc = sum(newcases), prev = sum(sick), prev_obs = sum(prev_obs), dead = sum(dead)), by = .(scenario, year)]
  wide <- dcast(agg, year ~ scenario, value.var = c("pop", "inc", "prev", "prev_obs", "dead"))
  wide[, averted := dead_ref - dead_sap]
  st0 <- d$bs$states[[1]]; cv <- st0$coverage; tr <- st0$transitions; pd <- st0$p_rhd_death
  ef <- st0$effects; sg <- st0$surgery
  # GBD published counts (burden statement) and target-basis counts (model comparisons)
  g <- d$gbd[metric_name == "Number" & cause_name == "Rheumatic heart disease",
             .(val = sum(val)), by = .(measure = measure_name, year)]
  g_last <- max(g$year)
  pg <- d$pop[location == ct, .(pop = sum(Nx)), by = .(year, sex, grp = age_to_grp(age))]
  basis <- sc$spec$target_basis
  gb <- if (identical(basis, "number")) g else
    merge(d$gbd[metric_name == "Rate" & cause_name == "Rheumatic heart disease",
                .(measure = measure_name, year, sex = sex_name, grp = age_name, rate = val / 1e5)],
          pg, by = c("year", "sex", "grp"))[, .(val = sum(rate * pop)), by = .(measure, year)]
  # Layer-2 fit in the last calibration year, scored vs validation
  fl <- as.data.table(sc$fit_by_group_year); fl[, glo := grp_lo[age_group]]
  floor <- if (is.null(oc$death_target_age_min)) 0L else as.integer(oc$death_target_age_min)
  # childhood deaths: below the scoring floor when one is set, else under 20 (scored, shown as fit)
  kid <- if (floor > 0) floor else 20L
  cy <- as.integer(cal$meta$calib_year_end)
  rat <- function(f) f[, sum(model) / sum(target_used, na.rm = TRUE)]
  fit <- list(
    prev = rat(fl[year == cy & measure == "Prevalence"]), inc = rat(fl[year == cy & measure == "Incidence"]),
    dead_all = rat(fl[year == cy & measure == "Deaths"]), dead_scored = rat(fl[year == cy & measure == "Deaths" & glo >= floor]),
    gbd_prev = fl[year == cy & measure == "Prevalence", sum(target_used, na.rm = TRUE)],
    gbd_dead_adult = fl[year == cy & measure == "Deaths" & glo >= floor, sum(target_used, na.rm = TRUE)],
    gbd_dead_child = fl[year == cy & measure == "Deaths" & glo < kid, sum(target_used, na.rm = TRUE)],
    mod_dead_child = fl[year == cy & measure == "Deaths" & glo < kid, sum(model)],
    gbd_dead_all = fl[year == cy & measure == "Deaths", sum(target_used, na.rm = TRUE)])
  # stage stocks and flows
  stk <- s[, .(A = sum(A), B = sum(B), C = sum(C), D = sum(D)), by = .(scenario, year)]
  flw <- s[, .(AB = sum(A_to_B), BC = sum(B_to_C), CD = sum(C_to_D), dD = sum(rhd_deaths_D)), by = scenario]
  # service volumes and discounted incremental cost by component (08's definitions)
  vol <- s[, .(screened = sum(n_screened), diagnosed = sum(n_diagnosed),
               on_sap = sum(n_on_optimal_treatment), surgeries = sum(total_surgeries)), by = .(scenario, year)]
  cc <- vol[, .(screen = screened * ep$cost_screen_per_person, sap = on_sap * ep$cost_sap_per_year,
                surg = surgeries * ep$cost_surgery), by = .(scenario, year)]
  cc[, df := 1 / (1 + ep$disc_rate)^(year - dby)]
  ccw <- dcast(cc, year + df ~ scenario, value.var = c("screen", "sap", "surg"))
  comp <- ccw[, c(screen = sum((screen_sap - screen_ref) * df), sap = sum((sap_sap - sap_ref) * df),
                  surg = sum((surg_sap - surg_ref) * df))]
  es <- as.list(d$econ$summary[location == ct])
  inc <- as.data.table(d$econ$incremental)
  t50 <- inc[year <= ye, .(cost = sum(inc_cost * df), ben = sum(benefit_total * df), da = sum(deaths_avert))]
  check(abs(sum(comp) - es$total_cost) / abs(es$total_cost) < 1e-8, paste(ct, "cost recomputation differs from 08"),
        paste("re-run 08 for", ct))
  # revision bridge: the RETIRED definitions recomputed from this run (health identical in
  # every row). Retired screening = reach x whole population every year; retired valuation
  # = deaths averted x (VSL multiple + 1) x GDP per capita.
  alt <- dcast(s[, .(old = sum(pop * screen_coverage), new = sum(n_screened)), by = .(scenario, year)],
               year ~ scenario, value.var = c("old", "new"))
  alt <- merge(alt, inc[, .(year, df, deaths_avert, gdp_pc)], by = "year")
  pvc_old <- es$total_cost + alt[, sum(df * ep$cost_screen_per_person * ((old_sap - old_ref) - (new_sap - new_ref)))]
  pvb_old <- alt[, sum(df * deaths_avert * (ep$vsl_mult + 1) * gdp_pc)]
  bridge <- data.table(row_id = c("prev", "screen", "value", "both"),
                       cost = c(pvc_old, es$total_cost, pvc_old, es$total_cost),
                       ben = c(pvb_old, pvb_old, es$total_benefit, es$total_benefit))
  bridge[, bcr := fifelse(cost > 0, ben / cost, NA_real_)]
  sched <- st0$coverage$screen_schedule
  sby <- as.data.table(d$out$diag$screening_by_year)
  check(isTRUE(all.equal(cv$ref$surgery, cv$sap$surgery)), paste(ct, "surgery coverage differs by arm"))
  check(all(vapply(c("screen", "diagnosis", "treatment"), function(k) diff(range(cv$ref[[k]])) < 1e-12, NA)),
        paste(ct, "reference cascade is not constant"))
  hr <- c(A_to_B = ef$sap_hr_A_to_B, B_to_C = ef$sap_hr_B_to_C, C_to_D = ef$sap_hr_C_to_D)
  c_tgt <- max(cv$sap$eff_protection); c_ref <- cv$ref$eff_protection[1]
  first_eff <- wide[abs(averted) > 1e-6, suppressWarnings(min(year))]
  list(
    ct = ct, y0 = y0, y1 = y1, ye = ye, yy = yy, wide = wide, agg = agg, g = g, gb = gb, g_last = g_last,
    st = stk, flw = flw, vol = vol, comp = comp, es = es, inc = inc, t50 = t50, ep = ep, dby = dby,
    bridge = bridge, sched = sched, sby = sby, vsl_b = ep$vsl_mult * ep$gni_pc_base, s_old_ye = alt[year == ye, old_sap],
    cv = cv, tr = tr, pd = pd, ef = ef, sg = sg, trend = meta$incidence_trend, hr = hr, c_tgt = c_tgt, c_ref = c_ref,
    cut_tgt = c_tgt * (1 - hr), cut_ref = c_ref * (1 - hr), first_eff = first_eff,
    averted = wide[, sum(averted)], averted_ye = wide[year <= ye, sum(averted)],
    rel_cum = 1 - wide[, sum(dead_sap) / sum(dead_ref)],
    rate_red_ye = wide[year == ye, 1 - (dead_sap / pop_sap) / (dead_ref / pop_ref)],
    deaths_y0 = wide[year == y0, dead_ref], prev_y0 = wide[year == y0, prev_obs_ref],
    inc_diff = wide[, sum(inc_sap) - sum(inc_ref)], inc_ref_cum = wide[, sum(inc_ref)],
    prev_end_ref = wide[year == y1, prev_ref], prev_end_sap = wide[year == y1, prev_sap],
    gbd_prev = g[measure == "Prevalence" & year == g_last, val],
    gbd_deaths = g[measure == "Deaths" & year == g_last, val],
    gbd_deaths_basis = gb[measure == "Deaths" & year == g_last, val],
    gbd_prev_basis = gb[measure == "Prevalence" & year == g_last, val],
    D_chg = stk[scenario == "sap" & year == y1, D] / stk[scenario == "ref" & year == y1, D] - 1,
    nonbinding = isTRUE(all.equal(cv$sap$eff_treatment, cv$sap$treatment)) &&
                 isTRUE(all.equal(cv$ref$eff_treatment, cv$ref$treatment)),
    adh_one = all(abs(c(cv$ref$adherence, cv$sap$adherence) - 1) < 1e-12),
    cal = cal, sc = sc, oc = oc, eda = eda, bp = bp, fl = fl, floor = floor, kid = kid, cy = cy, fit = fit,
    prev_obs = prev_obs, basis = basis, ptab = as.data.table(sc$parameters),
    ident = as.data.table(sc$identifiability))
}
R <- setNames(lapply(COUNTRIES, summarise_country), COUNTRIES)
I <- R$Indonesia; U <- R$Uganda
Y0 <- I$y0; Y1 <- I$y1; YE <- I$ye; CY <- I$cy; FLOOR <- I$floor; KID <- I$kid
basis_label <- if (identical(I$basis, "number")) "GBD published counts" else "GBD rate $\\times$ WPP population"

# ---- Optional project worksheets (read-only; described as unavailable if absent)
read_sheet <- function(...) {
  p <- file.path(ROOT, ...)
  if (!file.exists(p) || !requireNamespace("readxl", quietly = TRUE)) return(NULL)
  as.data.frame(readxl::read_excel(p, sheet = 1, col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text",
                                   .name_repair = "minimal"))
}
num_cells <- function(v) { v <- trimws(unlist(v)); as.numeric(v[!is.na(v) & grepl("^[0-9.]+([eE][-+]?[0-9]+)?$", v)]) }
tp_map <- c("Stage A to Normal" = "p_A_to_no_rhd", "Stage A to B" = "p_A_to_B", "Stage B to A" = "p_B_to_A",
            "Stage B to C" = "p_B_to_C", "Stage C to B" = "p_C_to_B", "Stage C to D" = "p_C_to_D",
            "Stage D to C" = "p_D_to_C")
tp_lab <- c(p_A_to_no_rhd = "A $\\rightarrow$ no RHD", p_A_to_B = "A $\\rightarrow$ B",
            p_B_to_A = "B $\\rightarrow$ A", p_B_to_C = "B $\\rightarrow$ C", p_C_to_B = "C $\\rightarrow$ B",
            p_C_to_D = "C $\\rightarrow$ D", p_D_to_C = "D $\\rightarrow$ C")
lit_x <- read_sheet("dev", "Summary progression rates_Sep26Update.xlsx")
LIT <- if (is.null(lit_x)) NULL else {
  lab <- trimws(lit_x[[1]]); t2 <- grep("^Table 2", lab); t3 <- grep("^Table 3", lab)
  rows <- seq(t2 + 1, t3 - 1)
  rbindlist(lapply(names(tp_map), function(nm) {
    v <- num_cells(lit_x[rows[lab[rows] == nm][1], -1])
    data.table(par = tp_map[[nm]], n = length(v), lo = min(v), hi = max(v))
  }))
}
dd_x <- read_sheet("dev", "TP Stage D to death_RHDparameters.xlsx")
DPROXY <- if (is.null(dd_x)) NULL else {
  hdr <- as.character(unlist(dd_x[1, ])); jl <- grep("A/D1", hdr, fixed = TRUE); jg <- grep("A/D2", hdr, fixed = TRUE)
  rbindlist(lapply(COUNTRIES, function(ct) {
    r <- which(trimws(dd_x[[1]]) == ct & trimws(dd_x[[2]]) == "All ages")[1]
    data.table(ct = ct, lit = as.numeric(dd_x[r, jl]) / 100, gbd_hf = as.numeric(dd_x[r, jg]) / 100)
  }))
}

kb <- function(df, align, widths = NULL, font = NULL) {
  k <- kbl(df, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = align, escape = FALSE, linesep = "",
           row.names = FALSE)
  k <- kable_styling(k, position = "center", font_size = font)
  if (!is.null(widths)) for (i in seq_along(widths)) if (!is.na(widths[i])) k <- column_spec(k, i, width = widths[i])
  k
}
```

## We ask whether scaling up echo screening and prophylaxis is worth its cost

1. **Health:** how many rheumatic heart disease (RHD) deaths does scale-up avert in Indonesia and Uganda, `r Y0`–`r Y1`?
2. **Services and cost:** what screening, prophylaxis and surgery does it add, at what cost?
3. **Value:** does the monetised benefit exceed the incremental cost?

\medskip

Scope: national, both sexes, ages 0–100+; secondary prevention only.

::: notes
Time: 1.0 min (cumulative 1.5). Lead with the decision, not an agenda. Out of scope: primary prevention, an acute rheumatic fever (ARF) state, heart-failure management. Transition: why the question matters now.
:::

## About `r fmt_f(TOT_PREV / 1e6, 1)` million people live with RHD in the two countries, and `r cov_word` prophylaxis

\bignumber{`r fmt_f(TOT_PREV / 1e6, 2)` million}{people living with RHD in Indonesia and Uganda, `r I$g_last`}

\medskip

Baseline optimal-treatment coverage in the model: \prov{`r fmt_cov(I$cv$ref$treatment[1])`} in Indonesia, \prov{`r fmt_cov(U$cv$ref$treatment[1])`} in Uganda.

\srcline GBD 2023 RHD prevalence, published counts summed over age and sex (Indonesia `r fmt_n(I$gbd_prev)`; Uganda `r fmt_n(U$gbd_prev)`). Amber marks provisional assumptions throughout.

::: notes
Time: 1.25 min (cumulative 2.75). GBD reports `r fmt_n(I$gbd_deaths)` RHD deaths in Indonesia and `r fmt_n(U$gbd_deaths)` in Uganda in `r I$g_last`. The coverage figures are model starting assumptions, not survey estimates. Transition: what the model builds on and where it stops.
:::

# How the model works

## Four linked steps turn GBD and WPP inputs into health and economic contrasts

\srcline GBD supplies the targets of both layers; both use WPP population as the denominator. Layer 2, the bridge and both arms run the same annual engine. SAP: secondary antibiotic prophylaxis. VSL: value of a statistical life.

::: notes
Time: 1.5 min (cumulative 5.5). Read left to right. GBD supplies rates and calibration targets; WPP supplies the population. Layer 1 is an aggregate proxy whose incidence multipliers only start the Layer-2 search. Layer 2 jointly fits incidence corrections, transitions and stage-D mortality with the production engine. The calibrated `r CY` state is projected through the bridge years to `r Y0`; it is not reset to GBD prevalence. The two arms differ only in the cascade. Transition: the state map itself.
:::

WHF restricts stage A to people aged 20 or younger; the model lets adults enter A, with separate adult progression and remission multipliers. `r if (D_ONLY) "RHD deaths occur only from stage D, a provisional structural choice that needs clinical review." else "RHD deaths can occur from mild stages, which collaborators have questioned."` Transition: how population enters and leaves.
:::

## Population is exogenous: WPP fixes each age–sex cell, and RHD stocks age within it

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Held fixed outside the model**

- Population $P_t$: WPP 2024, ages 0–100+, two sexes
- Background deaths: GBD all-cause minus RHD (held at `r D$Indonesia$bs$meta$RATE_BASE_YEAR` after calibration)
- Incidence: Layer-2 `r I$bp$ir_anchor_year` rate per susceptible $\times$ trend$^{\,t-`r I$bp$ir_anchor_year`}$
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Evolved by the model**

- Stocks A–D by age and sex
- Susceptible pool $= P_t - (A+B+C+D)$
- Annual cycles, `r Y0`–`r Y1`
- `r Y0` stock: calibrated `r CY` state, bridged forward
:::
::::

\srcline Incidence trend: \prov{`r fmt_f(I$trend, 3)`} per year (Indonesia), \prov{`r fmt_f(U$trend, 3)`} (Uganda). The `r Y0` stock is `r fmt_n(sum(sapply(D$Indonesia$bs$states[[1]]$seed, sum)))` (Indonesia) and `r fmt_n(sum(sapply(D$Uganda$bs$states[[1]]$seed, sum)))` (Uganda) people with RHD.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 8.25). Births and migration come from WPP, not from the model; the no-RHD pool absorbs them. Age 0 starts with no RHD; the 100+ group is open. Background mortality is the same for every state. WPP's own mortality and fertility assumptions shape the population but are not disease-engine inputs. The `r Y0` stock is not reset to GBD prevalence or to a fixed stage split. Transition: how competing exits are computed.
:::

## Competing exits are split on the hazard scale, so every stock balances exactly

Each stage faces several annual risks at once; converting them to hazards keeps every outflow non-negative.

$$
p_{s\to e}=\Big(1-e^{-H_s}\Big)\,\textcolor{wbblue}{\frac{h_e}{H_s}},\qquad
h_e=-\ln\left(1-p_e\right),\qquad H_s=\sum_{e\in\mathcal{E}_s} h_e
$$

Stage $s$ keeps the share $e^{-H_s}$. $\mathcal{E}_s$ holds the exits available from $s$ — for stage A: to no RHD, to B, `r if (D_ONLY) "other-cause death (its RHD-death hazard is exactly zero)" else "RHD death, other-cause death"`. All probabilities are per year.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 9.0). Intuition: if two risks compete, each claims a share of the total exit proportional to its hazard. No clipping is needed, and outflows plus the stay share sum to one. A zero probability has a zero hazard, so `r if (D_ONLY) "stages A to C produce exactly no RHD deaths" else "a stage with no risk of an event never loses anyone to it"`. The same function runs in calibration, the bridge and the projection. Transition: how one year is assembled.
:::

## Each year draws incidence from the susceptible pool, applies exits, then ages survivors

$$
A_{t+1}(a{+}1)=A_t(a)\,e^{-H_A}+B_t(a)\,p_{B\to A}+\textcolor{wbblue}{W_t(a)\,p_{W\to A}}
$$

$A_t(a)$: stage-A persons aged $a$ entering year $t$, for each sex. $W_t=P_t-(A_t+B_t+C_t+D_t)$: the susceptible pool, where incidence competes with other-cause death to give $p_{W\to A}$. Stages B–D follow the same form.

::: notes
Time: 1.0 min (cumulative 10.0). Ordering: stocks enter the year already aged; within-year flows compete; year-end stocks collect stays and inflows; then everyone ages. Deaths, incident cases and service volumes are within-year flows. For comparison with GBD, prevalence is observed as `r switch(I$prev_obs, mid = "the mean of the start and end stocks", start = "the start stock", end = "the end stock")`. The full four-stage system is in backup. Transition: what feeds these equations.
:::

## Effects, costs and valuation rest on literature and provisional values

```{r tab-inputs-2}
in2 <- data.frame(
  Input = c("SAP effect", "Adherence", "Surgery effect", "Cascade targets", "Screening schedule",
            "Unit costs", "GNI per capita", "VSL, discounting"),
  Value = c(if (PROG) paste0("HR ", paste(fmt_f(I$hr, 2), collapse = " / ")) else paste0(fmt_pct(I$ef$sap_rrr_rhd_death), " fewer RHD deaths"),
            if (I$adh_one && U$adh_one) "1 in both arms" else "Arm trajectories",

            "Screening, SAP, surgery",
            paste0("World Bank, ", I$ep$gni_pc_base_year),
            paste0(I$ep$vsl_mult, "$\\times$ GNI pc; ", fmt_pct(I$ep$disc_rate))),
  Role = c(if (PROG) "A$\\rightarrow$B, B$\\rightarrow$C, C$\\rightarrow$D" else "Multiplies RHD death",
           "Scales protection", "Scaled by reach", paste("Scale-up by", YE), "Encounters per year",
           "Cost per service", "Anchors VSL", "Benefits and costs"),
  Status = c("\\prov{Provisional}", "\\prov{No attenuation}", "Literature", "Policy scenario", "\\prov{Assumption}",
```

\srcline Targets: screening reach / diagnosis / SAP coverage. Screening ages: WHO 2024 supports 5--19; the adult window and frequencies are assumptions. Adherence 1 = no further attenuation.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 11.5). `r if (PROG) "The A to B and B to C hazard ratios convert GOAL-trial arm risks in children with latent RHD (curated in the collaborators' workbook; the trial is not in the project bibliography) under a provisional mapping of trial categories to WHF A and B. The C to D value of 0.45 is an assumption carried from @Coates2021, who applied it to progression to heart failure." else "The 55 percent effect follows @Coates2021, where it applies to progression."` Unit-cost sources and price year are not recorded in the pipeline. Transition: how the stage dynamics were calibrated.
:::

## Calibration fits incidence, transitions and stage-D mortality jointly inside the production engine

:::: columns
::: {.column width="47%"}
**Layer 1: aggregate proxy** (`r I$cal$meta$calib_year_start`–`r I$cal$meta$calib_year_end`)

- Well–sick–dead, no remission; GBD counts
- `r 2L * length(I$cal$meta$bands)` multipliers per sex: incidence, mortality
- Inverse-variance weights `r if (isTRUE(I$cal$layer1$optimizer_diagnostics$used_iv_weights)) "on" else "off"`
- Role: \prov{start values only}
:::
::: {.column width="51%"}
**Layer 2: joint, production engine** (scored `r I$oc$match_from`–`r CY`)

- Prevalence : deaths weight `r fmt_f(I$oc$prev_death_ratio, 1)` : 1; deaths `r if (FLOOR > 0) paste0("age ", FLOOR, "+") else "all ages"`
- Free: `r nrow(I$ptab)` parameters (`r sum(grepl("^alpha", I$ptab$parameter))` incidence $\alpha$, `r sum(grepl("^p_", I$ptab$parameter))` transitions, `r sum(grepl("mD|adult", I$ptab$parameter))` other)
- Zero-start burn-in, `r I$sc$priors$burn_years` cycles; IV weights `r if (isTRUE(I$oc$iv_weights$used)) "on" else "off"`
- Priors: mortality $\lambda$ `r fmt_f(I$oc$lambda_prior_mortality, 2)`, structure `r fmt_f(I$oc$lambda_prior_structural, 2)`
:::
::::

::: notes
Time: 1.0 min (cumulative 12.5). Despite its script name, Layer 1 is no longer a random search: it is a bounded multi-start fit of an aggregate proxy, and its incidence multipliers only start the Layer-2 search. Layer 2 runs the real engine with reference care applied inside the objective, so the fitted parameters are untreated natural history and care is applied once. The final Layer-2 incidence is saved and used by the projection without re-applying any correction. Years `r I$cal$meta$calib_year_start` to `r I$oc$match_from - 1L` are projected but carry zero weight. Inverse-variance weights are separate settings in the two layers, and GBD intervals are not independent errors. Transition: how well it fits.
:::

The tolerances are labels, not acceptance tests. Parameters at a bound: `r if (length(I$sc$bounds$boundary_hits)) gsub("_", " ", paste(I$sc$bounds$boundary_hits, collapse = ", ")) else "none"` (Indonesia), `r if (length(U$sc$bounds$boundary_hits)) gsub("_", " ", paste(U$sc$bounds$boundary_hits, collapse = ", ")) else "none"` (Uganda). \srcline `r if (FLOOR > 0) paste0("Under-", FLOOR, " death cells are masked from the loss and kept as validation") else "No death cells are masked: deaths at every age enter the loss"`; the age floor is read from the saved calibration.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 14.25). A natural history entered through stage A, with deaths only from stage D, cannot generate GBD's childhood RHD deaths without an acute or rapidly fatal childhood pathway that the model does not have. `r if (FLOOR > 0) "Scoring those cells forced faster progression at every age. The exclusion is a documented observation choice flagged for clinical review, not a clinically validated decision" else "This run scores those cells, so the optimiser trades them off against adult prevalence and deaths; compare with the age-20 floor run before choosing a primary specification"`, and it is a structural limitation of the current model. Transition: the stage-D mortality level.
:::

## Fitted stage-D mortality is `r fmt_pct(I$pd[["D"]], 1)` (Indonesia) and `r fmt_pct(U$pd[["D"]], 1)` (Uganda) per year, `r mD_rel(I)` and `r mD_rel(U)` their provisional priors

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 15.0). The prior centres are pooled workbook proxies, GBD RHD deaths divided by a GBD heart-failure-due-to-RHD stock; they are not validated annual transitions. Age-stratified workbook values are not implemented. The realised risk is lower than the fitted value because reference-arm surgery and competing other-cause death act on the same stock. The heart-failure proxy share is shown for orientation and is not a calibration target. Transition: what the fit does and does not identify.
:::

## `r IDENT_TITLE`

```{r tab-ident}
id_par <- c("p_A_to_no_rhd", "p_A_to_B", "p_B_to_A", "p_B_to_C", "p_C_to_B", "p_C_to_D", "log_mD",
            "log_adult_prog_mult", "log_adult_remission_mult")
id_lab <- c(unname(tp_lab[id_par[1:6]]), "Stage-D mortality", "Adult progression multiplier", "Adult remission multiplier")
cell <- function(dt, p) { r <- dt[parameter == p]
  if (!nrow(r)) return("--")
  v <- fmt_f(r$flatness)
  if (r$status != "data-identified") paste0("\\prov{\\textbf{", v, "}}") else v }
id_tab <- data.frame(Parameter = id_lab,
                     Indonesia = vapply(id_par, function(p) cell(I$ident, p), ""),
                     Uganda = vapply(id_par, function(p) cell(U$ident, p), ""))
kb(id_tab, "lrr", widths = c("5cm", "2.6cm", "2.6cm"), font = 9)
```

\srcline Flatness: share of a parameter's range within the near-optimal band, others held at the optimum; amber = flagged flat. Incidence multipliers in backup.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 15.75). Low flatness means the penalised objective rises when one parameter moves alone. That is weaker than joint identification: correlated parameters can trade off, and priors add curvature. Only `r I$oc$n_starts` random starts plus the prior centre, Layer-1 and prevalence-first starts were run. No usable echo stage targets exist for either country, so the stage split is partially identified. Transition: the comparison the arms make.
:::

# What the comparison changes

## Only the care cascade differs between arms; surgery coverage is identical in both

```{r tab-scen}
ramp <- function(cv, k) paste0(fmt_cov(cv$sap[[k]][1]), " $\\rightarrow$ ", fmt_cov(max(cv$sap[[k]])))
adh <- function(cv, a) paste0(fmt_f(cv[[a]]$adherence[1]), if (abs(diff(range(cv[[a]]$adherence))) > 1e-12) paste0("$\\rightarrow$", fmt_f(cv[[a]]$adherence[length(cv[[a]]$adherence)])) else "")
sc_tab <- data.frame(
  Step = c(paste0("Screening reach (ages ", SCHED_AGES, ")"), "Diagnosis (people with RHD)",
           "SAP (all prevalent RHD)", "Adherence modifier", "Surgery (C, D in need)"),
  ir = c(fmt_cov(I$cv$ref$screen[1]), fmt_cov(I$cv$ref$diagnosis[1]), fmt_cov(I$cv$ref$treatment[1]), adh(I$cv, "ref"), fmt_cov(I$cv$ref$surgery[1])),
  is = c(ramp(I$cv, "screen"), ramp(I$cv, "diagnosis"), ramp(I$cv, "treatment"), adh(I$cv, "sap"), fmt_cov(I$cv$sap$surgery[1])),
  ur = c(fmt_cov(U$cv$ref$screen[1]), fmt_cov(U$cv$ref$diagnosis[1]), fmt_cov(U$cv$ref$treatment[1]), adh(U$cv, "ref"), fmt_cov(U$cv$ref$surgery[1])),
  us = c(ramp(U$cv, "screen"), ramp(U$cv, "diagnosis"), ramp(U$cv, "treatment"), adh(U$cv, "sap"), fmt_cov(U$cv$sap$surgery[1])))
names(sc_tab) <- c("Cascade step (denominator)", "Reference", "Scale-up", "Reference", "Scale-up")
kb(sc_tab, "lrrrr", widths = c("4.3cm", "1.6cm", "2.1cm", "1.6cm", "2.1cm")) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Indonesia" = 2, "Uganda" = 2))
```

\srcline Scale-up ramps linearly from `r Y0` to `r YE`, then holds to `r Y1`. Surgery need per year: `r fmt_cov(I$sg$frac_C_requiring_surgery)` of C and `r fmt_cov(I$sg$frac_D_requiring_surgery)` of D (Indonesia); `r fmt_cov(U$sg$frac_C_requiring_surgery)` and `r fmt_cov(U$sg$frac_D_requiring_surgery)` (Uganda).

::: notes
Time: 1.5 min (cumulative 17.25). Confirmed in the saved inputs: the reference cascade is constant and surgery coverage is the same in both arms, so surgery shapes levels but not the contrast. An adherence modifier of 1 means no further attenuation of effective treatment; it is not an assumed improvement. The diagnosis and SAP denominators are the whole prevalent RHD stock at every age, so SAP continues between screenings and after people age out of the screening windows. Screening reach is the share of the scheduled encounters delivered, not a share of the whole population. Transition: how coverage evolves over time.
:::

## Treatment coverage reaches `r fmt_cov(max(I$cv$sap$treatment))` by `r YE` and then holds; `r if (I$nonbinding && U$nonbinding) "screening never constrains it" else "the earlier cascade steps constrain it in some years"`

```{r fig-coverage, fig.height = 2.15}
cov_dt <- rbindlist(lapply(COUNTRIES, function(ct) {
  cv <- R[[ct]]$cv; yy <- R[[ct]]$yy
  rbind(data.table(country = ct, year = yy, series = "Screening reach, scale-up", v = cv$sap$screen),
        data.table(country = ct, year = yy, series = "Effective protection, scale-up", v = cv$sap$eff_protection),
        data.table(country = ct, year = yy, series = "Effective protection, reference", v = cv$ref$eff_protection))
}))
lab_dt <- cov_dt[year == lab_year(I$yy, 0.7)][, .(country, year, v, series)]
lab_dt[, v := v + 0.07]
ggplot(cov_dt, aes(year, v, colour = series, linetype = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = lab_dt, aes(label = series), family = "Calibri", size = 3, hjust = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ country) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Screening reach, scale-up" = col_sap, "Effective protection, scale-up" = col_sap,
                                 "Effective protection, reference" = col_ref)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Screening reach, scale-up" = "22", "Effective protection, scale-up" = "solid",
                                   "Effective protection, reference" = "solid")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(c(Y0, YE, Y1))) +
  theme_deck
```

\srcline Effective protection = min(reach, diagnosis, SAP coverage) $\times$ adherence, a simplifying reach ceiling, not a measured cascade`r if (I$nonbinding && U$nonbinding) "; here it equals nominal treatment coverage" else ""``r if (I$adh_one && U$adh_one) " (adherence 1)" else ""`.

::: notes
Time: 1.25 min (cumulative 18.5). `r if (I$nonbinding && U$nonbinding) "Because screening and diagnosis targets exceed the treatment target at every year, the cascade minimum never binds; health effects run entirely through treatment coverage, and screening affects only cost." else "The cascade minimum binds in some years, so screening and diagnosis also limit health effects."` That is a property of the current parameters, not of the engine. The minimum is kept because it reproduces the reference care in the calibration; it is not a screening-only route to treatment, and clinical diagnosis outside screening is subsumed in SAP coverage. The screening frequencies never enter this line: they set encounter volumes and cost only. Transition: the mechanism through which treatment acts.
:::

## `r if (PROG) paste0("At target coverage SAP cuts the A", "$\\rightarrow$", "B, B", "$\\rightarrow$", "C and C", "$\\rightarrow$", "D hazards by ", fmt_pct(I$cut_tgt[["A_to_B"]]), ", ", fmt_pct(I$cut_tgt[["B_to_C"]]), " and ", fmt_pct(I$cut_tgt[["C_to_D"]])) else "SAP scales every stage's RHD death probability down in proportion to coverage"`

```{r sap-eq, results = "asis"}
if (PROG) {
  cat("$$\nh_{ij}(c_t)=h_{ij}(0)\\Big[1-\\textcolor{wbblue}{c_t\\,(1-\\mathrm{HR}_{ij})}\\Big],\\qquad c_t=c^{\\mathrm{tx}}_t\\,a_t,\\qquad c^{\\mathrm{tx}}_t=\\min\\big(c^{\\mathrm{scr}}_t,c^{\\mathrm{dx}}_t,c^{\\mathrm{trt}}_t\\big)\n$$\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("$h_{ij}$: annual hazard of progression $i\\rightarrow j$. HR = %s (A$\\rightarrow$B), %s (B$\\rightarrow$C), %s (C$\\rightarrow$D). $a_t$: adherence modifier. A population-average hazard approximation; no direct effect on mortality or incidence.\n",
              fmt_f(I$hr[["A_to_B"]], 3), fmt_f(I$hr[["B_to_C"]], 3), fmt_f(I$hr[["C_to_D"]], 3)))
} else {
  cat("$$\n\\tilde m_{s,t}=m_s\\Big(1-\\textcolor{wbblue}{\\rho\\,c_t}\\Big)\n$$\n\n")
  cat(sprintf("$\\rho$ = %s: legacy direct-mortality comparator.\n", fmt_f(I$ef$sap_rrr_rhd_death)))
}
```

::: notes
Time: 1.25 min (cumulative 19.75). `r if (PROG) paste0("The reference arm keeps a small effect: its hazards fall by ", fmt_pct(I$cut_ref[["A_to_B"]], 1), ", ", fmt_pct(I$cut_ref[["B_to_C"]], 1), " and ", fmt_pct(I$cut_ref[["C_to_D"]], 1), " in Indonesia and ", fmt_pct(U$cut_ref[["A_to_B"]], 1), ", ", fmt_pct(U$cut_ref[["B_to_C"]], 1), " and ", fmt_pct(U$cut_ref[["C_to_D"]], 1), " in Uganda. Mortality falls only because fewer people reach stage D, so the effect lags coverage. The legacy 55 percent direct-mortality mechanism is kept only as a comparator.") else "The reference arm keeps a small SAP effect."` Surgery also scales C to D and stage-D death by one minus its effect times its reach; that is equal across arms. Transition: how volumes become costs.
:::

## Costs are unit prices times modelled volumes; screening is priced per scheduled encounter at ages `r SCHED_AGES`

```{r tab-costs}
co_tab <- data.frame(
  Service = c("Echo screening", "Diagnosis", "SAP (optimal treatment)", "Valve surgery"),
  Volume = c(paste0("Reach $\\times\\,[", SCHED_TEX, "]$"), "Coverage $\\times$ prevalent RHD",
             "Coverage $\\times$ all prevalent RHD", "Need $\\times$ coverage $\\times$ C, D"),
  i = c(paste0("\\prov{", fmt_usd(I$ep$cost_screen_per_person, 2), "}"), "\\prov{not costed}",
        paste0("\\prov{", fmt_usd(I$ep$cost_sap_per_year), "}"), paste0("\\prov{", fmt_usd(I$ep$cost_surgery), "}")),
  u = c(paste0("\\prov{", fmt_usd(U$ep$cost_screen_per_person, 2), "}"), "\\prov{not costed}",
        paste0("\\prov{", fmt_usd(U$ep$cost_sap_per_year), "}"), paste0("\\prov{", fmt_usd(U$ep$cost_surgery), "}")))
names(co_tab) <- c("Service", "Annual volume", "Indonesia", "Uganda")
kb(co_tab, "llrr", widths = c("3.3cm", "4.7cm", "2.1cm", "2.1cm"))
```

\srcline Unit costs per screening encounter, per person-year on SAP and per surgery; sources and price year are not recorded in the pipeline. $P_{a\text{--}b}$: population aged $a$--$b$, both sexes. Implied perspective: programme delivery cost.

::: notes
Time: 1.5 min (cumulative 21.25). Screening is scheduled: `r SCHED` screens per person across each window, so each person-year in a window carries a fraction of an encounter. These are expected annual volumes of a programme spread across the window, not unique people or individual screening dates. WHO 2024 supports echo screening at ages 5 to 19 in moderate- or high-prevalence settings (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK609692/); the adult window and both frequencies are scenario assumptions. SAP is costed on prevalent RHD at every age times coverage, so it continues between screenings; eligibility, duration and retention are not modelled. Adherence lowers protection, not cost. Diagnosis is counted but carries no cost. Transition: how benefits are valued.
:::

## Each death averted is valued at a VSL anchored on GNI per capita and grown with GDP per capita

- Benefit$_t$ = deaths averted$_t$ $\times$ VSL$_t$; VSL$_t$ = `r I$ep$vsl_mult` $\times$ GNI pc$_{`r I$ep$gni_pc_base_year`}$ $\times$ GDP pc$_t$ / GDP pc$_{`r I$ep$gni_pc_base_year`}$
- GNI per capita, World Bank Atlas method, `r I$ep$gni_pc_base_year`: `r fmt_usd(I$ep$gni_pc_base)` (Indonesia), `r fmt_usd(U$ep$gni_pc_base)` (Uganda); VSL `r fmt_usd(I$vsl_b)` and `r fmt_usd(U$vsl_b)`, growing `r fmt_pct(I$ep$gdp_growth, 1)` and `r fmt_pct(U$ep$gdp_growth, 1)` a year
- No separate GDP benefit: GDP per capita only carries VSL forward
- @Coates2021 used a VSL of roughly 30 times income <!-- src: Coates2021, manuscript pp. 6 and 11 -->

\begin{uncertaintyblock}{Provisional multiple}
The `r I$ep$vsl_mult`$\times$ multiple is carried over from the former GDP-based specification and has not been re-estimated for GNI.
\end{uncertaintyblock}

::: notes
Time: 1.25 min (cumulative 22.5). The former valuation added one year of GDP per capita to a GDP-based VSL for every death averted; that term could double count, and it is removed. VSL is now anchored on GNI per capita (World Bank WDI, Atlas method, current US dollars of `r I$ep$gni_pc_base_year`) and grown with a constant real GDP-per-capita growth assumption, which implies an income elasticity of one over time. Growth rates are scenario assumptions, not forecasts. VSL is in constant `r I$ep$gni_pc_base_year` US dollars; the unit-cost price year is undocumented. The valuation is per RHD death averted within the horizon, not life-years or QALYs. Transition: the decision metric.
:::

## The decision metric is the discounted benefit–cost ratio over `r Y0`–`r Y1`

$$
\mathrm{BCR}=\frac{\sum_{t}\delta_t\,\Delta D_t\,\mathrm{VSL}_t}{\sum_t\delta_t\,\Delta C_t},
\qquad \mathrm{VSL}_t=m\,\mathrm{GNIpc}_b\,(1+g)^{t-b},
\qquad \delta_t=(1+r)^{-(t-`r I$dby`)}
$$

$\Delta D_t$: RHD deaths averted (reference minus scale-up, signed). $\Delta C_t$: incremental cost in US\$; the ratio is defined only when its sum is positive, otherwise reported as cost-neutral or cost-saving. $m$ = `r I$ep$vsl_mult`; $b$ = `r I$ep$gni_pc_base_year`; $r$ = `r fmt_pct(I$ep$disc_rate)` for costs and benefits. Cost per death and per disability-adjusted life year (DALY) are secondary outputs (backup).

::: notes
Time: 1.25 min (cumulative 23.75). This is benefit–cost analysis, not cost-effectiveness analysis: health is monetised once, through VSL alone, and compared with incremental (not gross) programme cost. Transition: what the model projects, starting with whether the baseline is credible.
:::

# What the model projects

## Projected `r Y0` RHD deaths are `r rel_phrase(I$deaths_y0 / I$gbd_deaths_basis)` GBD `r I$g_last` in Indonesia and `r rel_phrase(U$deaths_y0 / U$gbd_deaths_basis)` in Uganda

```{r fig-validation, fig.height = 2.35}
val <- rbindlist(lapply(COUNTRIES, function(ct) {
  r <- R[[ct]]
  rbind(r$gb[measure %in% c("Prevalence", "Deaths") & year >= 2000,
             .(country = ct, measure, year, v = val, src = "GBD 2023")],
        r$agg[scenario == "ref", .(country = ct, measure = "Prevalence", year, v = prev_obs, src = "Model, reference")],
        r$agg[scenario == "ref", .(country = ct, measure = "Deaths", year, v = dead, src = "Model, reference")])
}))
val[, panel := factor(paste0(country, ": ", fifelse(measure == "Prevalence", "people living with RHD", "RHD deaths")),
                      levels = c("Indonesia: people living with RHD", "Uganda: people living with RHD",
                                 "Indonesia: RHD deaths", "Uganda: RHD deaths"))]
ggplot(val, aes(year, v, colour = src, linetype = src)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("GBD 2023" = col_gbd, "Model, reference" = col_ref)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("GBD 2023" = "solid", "Model, reference" = "22")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()),
                     limits = c(0, NA), n.breaks = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(c(2000, Y0, YE, Y1))) +
  theme_deck
```

\srcline Solid green: GBD 2023 (`r basis_label`), 2000–`r I$g_last`. Dashed grey: model reference arm, `r Y0`–`r Y1`; prevalence on the calibration's observation convention. All ages, both sexes.

::: notes
Time: 1.25 min (cumulative 25.0). The model enters `r Y0` with the bridged calibrated state, not with GBD prevalence: its `r Y0` prevalence is `r rel_phrase(I$prev_y0 / I$gbd_prev_basis)` GBD `r I$g_last` in Indonesia and `r rel_phrase(U$prev_y0 / U$gbd_prev_basis)` in Uganda. These comparisons span different years. Projected deaths include few childhood deaths, by construction. Every effect that follows is measured against this baseline. Transition: the health effect.
:::

## Scale-up averts about `r fmt_h(I$averted)` RHD deaths in Indonesia and `r fmt_h(U$averted)` in Uganda by `r Y1`

```{r fig-deaths, fig.height = 2.2}
dd <- rbindlist(lapply(COUNTRIES, function(ct) R[[ct]]$wide[, .(country = ct, year, ref = dead_ref, sap = dead_sap)]))
dl <- melt(dd, id.vars = c("country", "year"), variable.name = "arm", value.name = "v")
lab <- dl[year == lab_year(I$yy, 0.83)][, v := v * fifelse(arm == "ref", 1.12, 0.80)]
lab[, txt := fifelse(arm == "ref", "Reference", "Scale-up")]
ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(data = dd, aes(year, ymin = pmin(sap, ref), ymax = pmax(sap, ref)), fill = col_sap, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(data = dl, aes(year, v, colour = arm), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = lab, aes(year, v, label = txt, colour = arm), family = "Calibri", size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ country, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(ref = col_ref, sap = col_sap)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma, limits = c(0, NA), n.breaks = 4) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = unique(c(Y0, YE, Y1))) +
  theme_deck
```

\srcline Annual RHD deaths; shaded = difference between arms. Cumulative: `r fmt_pct(I$rel_cum)` (Indonesia) and `r fmt_pct(U$rel_cum)` (Uganda) of reference-arm RHD deaths, `r Y0`–`r Y1`.

::: notes
Time: 1.0 min (cumulative 26.0). Deaths first differ in `r I$first_eff` (Indonesia) and `r U$first_eff` (Uganda): `r if (PROG) "a progression effect needs time to reduce entry into stage D" else "the effect starts with coverage"`. Of the totals, `r fmt_h(I$averted_ye)` (Indonesia) and `r fmt_h(U$averted_ye)` (Uganda) occur by `r YE`. Deaths averted are counted within the horizon; some may be deferred beyond `r Y1` rather than prevented. Point estimates only. Transition: where the stock goes.
:::

## By `r Y1`, scale-up leaves stage D `r D_word(I)` in Indonesia and `r D_word(U)` in Uganda

```{r fig-stage, fig.height = 2.1}
sg <- rbindlist(lapply(COUNTRIES, function(ct) {
  st <- R[[ct]]$st[year == Y1]
  m <- melt(st, id.vars = c("scenario", "year"), variable.name = "stage", value.name = "n")
  w <- dcast(m, stage ~ scenario, value.var = "n")
  w[, .(country = ct, stage, pct = sap / ref - 1)]
}))
sg[, hi := stage == "D"]
ggplot(sg, aes(stage, pct, fill = hi)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::percent(pct, accuracy = 1), vjust = ifelse(pct >= 0, -0.4, 1.3)), family = "Calibri", size = 3.2) +
  facet_wrap(~ country) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = col_stage[["D"]], `FALSE` = "grey70")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0.18, 0.18))) +
  theme_deck
```

\srcline Prevalent cases by stage, scale-up vs reference, end of `r Y1`. Total prevalent RHD: `r chg_phrase(I$prev_end_sap, I$prev_end_ref, "higher", "lower", 1)` (Indonesia), `r chg_phrase(U$prev_end_sap, U$prev_end_ref, "higher", "lower", 1)` (Uganda).

::: notes
Time: 1.0 min (cumulative 27.0). `r if (PROG) "Slower progression keeps people in earlier stages, so later stages shrink and the stock shifts toward A." else "Survivors accumulate in the stages they occupy."` SAP has no direct effect on the incidence hazard, but cumulative incident cases are `r if (abs(I$inc_diff) < 0.5) "unchanged" else paste(fmt_n(abs(I$inc_diff)), if (I$inc_diff > 0) "higher" else "lower")` in Indonesia and `r if (abs(U$inc_diff) < 0.5) "unchanged" else paste(fmt_n(abs(U$inc_diff)), if (U$inc_diff > 0) "higher" else "lower")` in Uganda, because the susceptible pool differs between arms. The RHD death rate in `r YE` is `r fmt_pct(I$rate_red_ye)` (Indonesia) and `r fmt_pct(U$rate_red_ye)` (Uganda) lower. Transition: what the programme must deliver.
:::

## By `r YE` the scale-up delivers `r fmt_f(R$Indonesia$vol[scenario == "sap" & year == YE, screened] / 1e6, 1)` million screening encounters a year in Indonesia and keeps `r fmt_h(R$Indonesia$vol[scenario == "sap" & year == YE, on_sap])` on SAP

```{r tab-volumes}
vv <- function(ct, arm, k, f) f(R[[ct]]$vol[scenario == arm & year == YE][[k]])
fk <- function(x) fmt_h(x)
fm2 <- function(x) fmt_mn(x, 2)
vol_tab <- data.frame(
  q = c("Screening encounters", "Prevalent RHD diagnosed", "People on SAP (all ages)", "Valve surgeries"),
  a = c(vv("Indonesia", "ref", "screened", fm2), vv("Indonesia", "ref", "diagnosed", fk),
        vv("Indonesia", "ref", "on_sap", fk), vv("Indonesia", "ref", "surgeries", fmt_n)),
  b = c(vv("Indonesia", "sap", "screened", fm2), vv("Indonesia", "sap", "diagnosed", fk),
        vv("Indonesia", "sap", "on_sap", fk), vv("Indonesia", "sap", "surgeries", fmt_n)),
  c = c(vv("Uganda", "ref", "screened", fm2), vv("Uganda", "ref", "diagnosed", fk),
        vv("Uganda", "ref", "on_sap", fk), vv("Uganda", "ref", "surgeries", fmt_n)),
  d = c(vv("Uganda", "sap", "screened", fm2), vv("Uganda", "sap", "diagnosed", fk),
        vv("Uganda", "sap", "on_sap", fk), vv("Uganda", "sap", "surgeries", fmt_n)))
names(vol_tab) <- c(paste0("Per year, ", YE), "Reference", "Scale-up", "Reference", "Scale-up")
kb(vol_tab, "lrrrr", widths = c("3.9cm", "1.95cm", "1.95cm", "1.95cm", "1.95cm")) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Indonesia" = 2, "Uganda" = 2)) |>
  column_spec(c(3, 5), bold = TRUE)
```

\srcline Counts from the model's service trace; m = million. Encounters = reach $\times$ scheduled screens per person-year $\times$ population aged `r SCHED_AGES` (expected volumes, not unique people). Diagnosis and SAP volumes are shares of the prevalent RHD stock at all ages.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 27.75). Under the retired whole-population definition the Indonesian scale-up arm would have priced `r fmt_f(R$Indonesia$s_old_ye / 1e6, 0)` million screenings in `r YE`; the scheduled programme delivers `r fmt_pct(R$Indonesia$vol[scenario == "sap" & year == YE, screened] / R$Indonesia$s_old_ye, 1)` of that (Uganda `r fmt_pct(R$Uganda$vol[scenario == "sap" & year == YE, screened] / R$Uganda$s_old_ye, 1)`). SAP volumes do not depend on the screening schedule. Surgery volumes differ between arms only because the C and D stocks differ; surgery coverage is the same in both arms. Transition: what this costs.
:::

## Echo screening is `r fmt_pct(SH[1])` of Indonesia's and `r fmt_pct(SH[2])` of Uganda's discounted incremental cost

```{r fig-costs, fig.height = 1.7}
cdt <- rbindlist(lapply(COUNTRIES, function(ct) {
  cp <- R[[ct]]$comp
  data.table(country = ct, comp = factor(c("Screening", "SAP", "Surgery"), levels = rev(c("Screening", "SAP", "Surgery"))),
             v = c(cp[["screen"]], cp[["sap"]], cp[["surg"]]), tot = sum(cp))
}))
cdt[, share := v / tot]
cdt[, country := factor(country, levels = rev(COUNTRIES))]
tot_lab <- unique(cdt[, .(country, tot)])
ggplot(cdt, aes(share, country, fill = comp)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +

            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), colour = "white", family = "Calibri", size = 3.2) +
  geom_text(data = tot_lab, aes(x = 1.02, y = country, label = paste0("US$", formatC(tot / 1e9, format = "f", digits = 2), " bn")),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, family = "Calibri", size = 3.2) +

```

\srcline Discounted (`r fmt_pct(I$ep$disc_rate)`, base `r I$dby`) incremental cost, `r Y0`–`r Y1`, by component; surgery is `r fmt_pct(I$comp[["surg"]] / sum(I$comp), 1)` (Indonesia) and `r fmt_pct(U$comp[["surg"]] / sum(U$comp), 1)` (Uganda).

::: notes
Time: 1.0 min (cumulative 28.75). `r if (I$nonbinding && U$nonbinding) "Under these targets screening never limits effective treatment, so it carries cost but none of the health effect;" else "Screening carries cost and, in some years, limits effective treatment;"` `r if (max(SH) < 0.5) "with scheduled encounters, SAP person-years now carry most of the incremental cost, and screening's share depends on the assumed ages and frequencies." else "its assumed ages and frequencies remain the most consequential provisional assumption on the cost side."` Transition: the economic result.
:::

## Benefit–cost ratios are `r if (bcr_ok[1]) fmt_f(I$es$bcr) else "undefined"` in Indonesia and `r if (bcr_ok[2]) fmt_f(U$es$bcr) else "undefined"` in Uganda over `r Y0`–`r Y1`

```{r tab-econ}
ec_tab <- data.frame(
  q = c("Incremental cost", "Monetised benefit", "Net benefit", "Benefit–cost ratio", "RHD deaths averted (undiscounted)"),
  i = c(fmt_bn(I$es$total_cost), fmt_bn(I$es$total_benefit), fmt_bn(I$es$net_benefit),
        if (bcr_ok[1]) fmt_f(I$es$bcr) else "undefined", fmt_n(I$es$deaths_averted)),
  u = c(fmt_bn(U$es$total_cost), fmt_bn(U$es$total_benefit), fmt_bn(U$es$net_benefit),
        if (bcr_ok[2]) fmt_f(U$es$bcr) else "undefined", fmt_n(U$es$deaths_averted)))
names(ec_tab) <- c(paste0("Discounted to ", I$dby, " at ", fmt_pct(I$ep$disc_rate)), "Indonesia", "Uganda")
kb(ec_tab, "lrr", widths = c("6.5cm", "2.8cm", "2.8cm")) |> row_spec(4, bold = TRUE)
```

\srcline US\$; benefit = deaths averted $\times$ VSL only (`r I$ep$vsl_mult`$\times$ GNI per capita, `r I$ep$gni_pc_base_year`, grown with GDP per capita); unit-cost price year undocumented. Deterministic point estimates.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 29.5). The ratio is `r if (all(bcr_ok)) { if (I$es$bcr > U$es$bcr) "higher in Indonesia" else if (I$es$bcr < U$es$bcr) "higher in Uganda" else "the same in both countries" } else "undefined for at least one country"`. The two differ in costs, valuation (GNI per capita) and the size of the averted death toll. Transition: how the two corrections in this revision moved the ratios.
:::

## Pricing screening per scheduled encounter `r up_down(c(BR(I, "screen"), BR(U, "screen")), c(BR(I, "prev"), BR(U, "prev")), "raises", "lowers")` both ratios; the GNI-based, VSL-only valuation then `r up_down(c(BR(I, "both"), BR(U, "both")), c(BR(I, "screen"), BR(U, "screen")), "raises", "lowers")` them

```{r tab-bridge}
bc <- function(r, k, f) { b <- r$bridge[row_id == k]; f(b) }
bm <- function(x) fmt_n(x / 1e6)
br_tab <- data.frame(
  q = c("Retired definitions", "Screening correction only", "Valuation correction only", "Both (saved run)"),
  ic = vapply(c("prev", "screen", "value", "both"), function(k) bc(I, k, function(b) bm(b$cost)), ""),
  ib = vapply(c("prev", "screen", "value", "both"), function(k) bc(I, k, function(b) bm(b$ben)), ""),
  ir = vapply(c("prev", "screen", "value", "both"), function(k) bc(I, k, function(b) if (is.finite(b$bcr)) fmt_f(b$bcr) else "undef."), ""),
  uc = vapply(c("prev", "screen", "value", "both"), function(k) bc(U, k, function(b) bm(b$cost)), ""),
  ub = vapply(c("prev", "screen", "value", "both"), function(k) bc(U, k, function(b) bm(b$ben)), ""),
  ur = vapply(c("prev", "screen", "value", "both"), function(k) bc(U, k, function(b) if (is.finite(b$bcr)) fmt_f(b$bcr) else "undef."), ""))
names(br_tab) <- c("Discounted, US\\$ m", "Cost", "Benefit", "BCR", "Cost", "Benefit", "BCR")
kb(br_tab, "lrrrrrr", widths = c("4.1cm", "1.35cm", "1.35cm", "1.1cm", "1.35cm", "1.35cm", "1.1cm"), font = 9) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Indonesia" = 3, "Uganda" = 3)) |>
  row_spec(4, bold = TRUE)
```

\srcline Retired definitions recomputed from the saved run: screening = reach $\times$ whole population every year; benefit = deaths averted $\times$ (`r I$ep$vsl_mult` + 1) $\times$ GDP per capita. Deaths averted are identical in every row; the first row reproduces the pre-revision results.

::: notes
Time: 0.5 min (cumulative 30.0). Screening: with benefits fixed, a lower but still positive incremental cost raises the ratio; it reflects cheaper delivery, not greater effectiveness. Valuation: GNI per capita is `r fmt_usd(I$ep$gni_pc_base)` (Indonesia) and `r fmt_usd(U$ep$gni_pc_base)` (Uganda) against the former GDP-per-capita levels of `r fmt_usd(I$ep$gdp_pc_base)` and `r fmt_usd(U$ep$gdp_pc_base)`, and the extra year of GDP per capita is gone, so benefits are `r chg_phrase(I$es$total_benefit, I$bridge[row_id == "prev", ben], "higher", "lower")` (Indonesia) and `r chg_phrase(U$es$total_benefit, U$bridge[row_id == "prev", ben], "higher", "lower")` (Uganda). Net effect of the revision: `r fmt_f(BR(I, "prev"))` to `r fmt_f(BR(I, "both"))` (Indonesia) and `r fmt_f(BR(U, "prev"))` to `r fmt_f(BR(U, "both"))` (Uganda). Transition: how much the horizon matters.
:::

## Ending the horizon in `r YE`, as the abstract did, `r hz_word` the ratios to `r fmt_f(B50[1])` and `r fmt_f(B50[2])`

```{r tab-horizon}

                     a = hz(I, FALSE), b = hz(I, TRUE), c = hz(U, FALSE), d = hz(U, TRUE))
names(hz_tab) <- c("", paste0(Y0, "–", YE), paste0(Y0, "–", Y1), paste0(Y0, "–", YE), paste0(Y0, "–", Y1))
kb(hz_tab, "lrrrr", widths = c("3.9cm", "1.95cm", "1.95cm", "1.95cm", "1.95cm")) |>
  add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Indonesia" = 2, "Uganda" = 2)) |>
  row_spec(2, bold = TRUE)
```

\srcline `r Y0`–`r YE` columns are deck-only sums of the saved runs to `r YE`; the model runs forward only, so this equals a `r YE` run with the same inputs.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 30.75). `r if (PROG) "With a progression mechanism, deaths averted keep growing after the ramp while costs plateau, so the horizon matters a great deal." else "Benefits keep accruing after the ramp while costs plateau."` The submitted abstract used earlier runs and a different specification (backup). Transition: what is settled and what is not.
:::

## `r if (is.null(DPROXY)) "The stage-D mortality prior is a provisional proxy, not a validated transition" else paste0("Stage-D mortality depends on its proxy: the two definitions differ up to ", fmt_n(max(DPROXY$gbd_hf / DPROXY$lit)), "-fold")`

```{r tab-dproxy}
dp_tab <- data.frame(
  Country = COUNTRIES,
  fit = c(fmt_pct(I$pd[["D"]], 1), fmt_pct(U$pd[["D"]], 1)),
  pri = c(fmt_pct(I$sc$priors$mortality_centers[["D"]], 1), fmt_pct(U$sc$priors$mortality_centers[["D"]], 1)),
  lit = if (is.null(DPROXY)) rep("n/a", 2) else fmt_pct(DPROXY[match(COUNTRIES, ct), lit], 1),
  hf = if (is.null(DPROXY)) rep("n/a", 2) else fmt_pct(DPROXY[match(COUNTRIES, ct), gbd_hf], 1))
```

\srcline Worksheet rates divide GBD 2023 RHD deaths by an estimated stage-D count (a literature stage-D share, or GBD RHD heart-failure prevalence); collaborator worksheet, October 2026. All ages, both sexes.

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 32.25). The prior uses the heart-failure-proxy definition. The choice of proxy changes the stage-D level, the D share and therefore the deaths SAP can avert. Age-stratified values exist in the worksheet but rest on tiny denominators and are not used. Transition: the transition probabilities.

## `r if (is.null(LIT)) "Calibrated transitions cannot be compared with the literature worksheet at render time" else paste0(n_outside(I), " of Indonesia's and ", n_outside(U), " of Uganda's child-age transitions fall outside published ranges")`

```{r tab-lit}
tp_rows <- c("p_A_to_no_rhd", "p_A_to_B", "p_B_to_A", "p_B_to_C", "p_C_to_B", "p_C_to_D", "p_D_to_C")
flag <- function(v, p) { if (is.null(LIT)) return(fmt_f(v, 3)); r <- LIT[par == p]
  s <- fmt_f(v, 3); if (v < r$lo || v > r$hi) paste0("\\prov{\\textbf{", s, "}}") else s }
lit_tab <- data.frame(
  Transition = unname(tp_lab[tp_rows]),
  Lit = if (is.null(LIT)) rep("n/a", 7) else
    LIT[match(tp_rows, par), paste0(fmt_f(lo, 3), "–", fmt_f(hi, 3), " (", n, ")")],
  Indonesia = vapply(tp_rows, function(p) flag(I$tr[[p]], p), ""),
  Uganda = vapply(tp_rows, function(p) flag(U$tr[[p]], p), ""))
names(lit_tab) <- c("Annual probability", "Literature range (studies)", "Indonesia", "Uganda")
kb(lit_tab, "lrrr", widths = c("3.2cm", "4.2cm", "2.3cm", "2.3cm"))
```

\srcline Annualised ranges from the collaborators' September 2026 literature table; amber bold = outside the range. Values apply below age `r I$bp$age_structure$adult_age_cutoff`; adult hazards are scaled (backup).

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 33.0). The calibration bounds are the literature ranges widened. Parameters at a bound: `r if (length(I$sc$bounds$boundary_hits)) gsub("_", " ", paste(I$sc$bounds$boundary_hits, collapse = ", ")) else "none"` in Indonesia, `r if (length(U$sc$bounds$boundary_hits)) gsub("_", " ", paste(U$sc$bounds$boundary_hits, collapse = ", ")) else "none"` in Uganda. `r if (!pdc_on) "D to C is fixed at zero, although studies report regression from D." else ""` The table pools treated and untreated cohorts and different follow-up lengths. Transition: the evidence for the SAP effects.
:::

`r if (PROG) "Mapping trial categories to WHF stages A and B is provisional; no pathway-specific trial informs C to D." else "A mortality effect acts at once; a progression effect is delayed and works by preventing stage D."`

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 33.75). WHF recommends SAP for all stage C and D patients and for stage B patients aged 20 or younger; for stage A it depends on risk. The model applies the same hazard ratios at every age and to adults, beyond the trial population. Transition: the strongest objection overall.
:::

## The strongest objection: totals do not identify stages, and stages drive the benefit

:::: columns
::: {.column width="48%"}
**A skeptic would say**

GBD gives only total prevalence and deaths. Many stage splits fit about equally well, yet the SAP benefit depends on how many people progress toward stage D.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**What the evidence supports**

Results are conditional on one calibrated stage structure. Stage-level echo targets would pin the split; until then, ranges should come from sensitivity analysis.
:::
::::

::: notes
Time: 0.75 min (cumulative 34.5). Concede the point: the saved near-optimal solutions look tight, but they come from `r nrow(as.data.table(I$sc$convergence))` starts per country and are alternative optima, not a posterior. The model accepts a stage-prevalence target file; none exists for either country yet. Transition: the other limitations, with their direction.
:::

## Remaining limitations bias results in directions we can name

```{r tab-limits}
li_tab <- data.frame(
  L = c("Childhood deaths", "Transferability", "Adherence", "Screening schedule", "SAP eligibility",
        "Valuation", "Uncertainty"),
  E = c("Child deaths averted missing", "Direction unknown", if (I$adh_one && U$adh_one) "Effect per dollar high" else "Depends on trajectory",
        "Ages, frequency assumed", "Volume approximate", paste0(I$ep$vsl_mult, "$\\times$ GNI provisional"),
        "Spread unknown"),
  N = c("Acute childhood pathway; review", "Country cohort or registry data", "Adherence and retention data",
        "Programme ages, interval data", "Eligibility, duration, retention", "VSL and discount sensitivity",
        "Probabilistic, one-way analyses"))
names(li_tab) <- c("Limitation", "Likely effect on results", "What resolves it")
kb(li_tab, "lll", widths = c("3.7cm", "3.9cm", "5cm"))
```

::: notes
Time: 0.5 min (cumulative 35.0). Childhood: the model generates few under-`r KID` deaths, so any SAP benefit in children is understated. Transferability: priors are not from Indonesian or Ugandan cohorts. Adherence: `r if (I$adh_one && U$adh_one) "a modifier of 1 means effective treatment is fully protective, with no drop-off" else "the saved trajectories attenuate protection"`. Screening: only the 5 to 19 window has WHO support; encounters are expected volumes, not individual histories. SAP: prevalent RHD times coverage ignores guideline eligibility, prophylaxis duration, initiation, discontinuation and retention. Transition: the order of updates.
:::

## Five updates, in this order, should precede any investment conclusion

1. **Stage-D mortality and the childhood pathway** — deaths, stage mix, every result
2. **SAP stage mapping and the C$\rightarrow$D effect** — size and timing of benefit
3. **Echo stage targets** — the stage split the benefit depends on
4. **Screening ages, frequencies and unit-cost sources** — screening is `r fmt_pct(min(SH))`–`r fmt_pct(max(SH))` of incremental cost
5. **Sensitivity analyses** — adherence, weights, priors and the death-age floor

::: notes
Time: 0.5 min (cumulative 35.5). The first three change the health side and must precede costing refinements; the last makes uncertainty visible. Transition: the one sentence.
:::

## {.standout}

On current saved runs, scale-up returns `r if (bcr_ok[1]) paste0("US\\$", fmt_f(I$es$bcr, 1)) else "an undefined ratio"` (Indonesia) and `r if (bcr_ok[2]) paste0("US\\$", fmt_f(U$es$bcr, 1)) else "an undefined ratio"` (Uganda) per dollar through `r Y1`—but stage-D mortality, the SAP effects and the screening schedule must be settled first.

::: notes
Time: 0.25 min (cumulative 35.75). Pause here, then open the discussion.
:::

## Five collaborator decisions will define the next model version

1. Is stage-D-only RHD mortality acceptable, and which proxy should anchor its level?
2. How should childhood RHD deaths be represented: an acute pathway or an age-specific risk?
3. Do the GOAL trial effects map to WHF stages A and B, and what supports a C$\rightarrow$D effect?
4. Are the assumed screening windows and frequencies (`r SCHED`) right, and should adults be screened at all?
5. Should adherence below one be modelled, and from which data?

::: notes
Time: 4.25 min (cumulative 40.0). Leave this slide up for the discussion. Questions 1–3 change the health results; 4 sets the screening cost (`r fmt_pct(min(SH))`–`r fmt_pct(max(SH))` of incremental cost) but not the health effect; 5 scales the effect directly.
:::

## Within each annual cycle, the engine runs seven steps in a fixed order

1. Stocks A–D enter year $t$ already aged; $S_t=A_t+B_t+C_t+D_t$
2. Susceptible pool $W_t=\max(P_t-S_t,0)$; incidence competes with other-cause death
3. Coverage and adherence set protection $c_t$; surgery reach $f_C c^{\mathrm{surg}}$, $f_D c^{\mathrm{surg}}$
4. Each state splits its exits on the hazard scale
5. Year-end stocks collect stays and inflows; new cases join A
6. Record deaths and volumes: screening encounters $=c^{\mathrm{scr}}_t\sum_g (n_g/W_g)\,P_{g,t}$; diagnosed, on SAP $=c\,S_t$; surgeries $=f\,c^{\mathrm{surg}}\times$ C, D
7. Survivors age one year; age 0 starts empty; 100+ is open

## The four stage updates share one form; only stage D lacks an exit to a higher stage

$$
\begin{aligned}
A^{+}_t&=A_t\,e^{-H_A}+B_t\,p_{B\to A}+W_t\,p_{W\to A}\\
B^{+}_t&=B_t\,e^{-H_B}+A_t\,p_{A\to B}+C_t\,p_{C\to B}\\
C^{+}_t&=C_t\,e^{-H_C}+B_t\,p_{B\to C}+D_t\,p_{D\to C}\\
D^{+}_t&=D_t\,e^{-H_D}+C_t\,p_{C\to D}
\end{aligned}
$$

Each $p$ is the hazard-split outflow. Before the split, $p_{CD}$ is scaled by $1-\rho^{\mathrm{surg}}_{CD}f_C c^{\mathrm{surg}}$`r if (PROG) " and the A$\\rightarrow$B, B$\\rightarrow$C, C$\\rightarrow$D hazards by $1-c_t(1-\\mathrm{HR})$" else ""`; $m_D$ by $1-\rho^{\mathrm{surg}}_{Dd}f_D c^{\mathrm{surg}}$. RHD deaths $=\sum_s s_t\,p_{s\to\mathrm{RHD}}$. $A_{t+1}=\mathrm{shift}(A^{+}_t)$.

## Layer 1 minimises a weighted log error with priors and smoothness on band multipliers

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_1={}&\sum_{X\in\{I,P,D\}} w_X\,\frac{\sum_j \omega_j\big[\ln(X^{\mathrm{mod}}_j+\varepsilon)-\ln(X^{\mathrm{GBD}}_j+\varepsilon)\big]^2}{\sum_j\omega_j}\\
&+\lambda\sum_g\Big[\frac{\eta_g^2}{\sigma_\alpha^2}+\frac{\zeta_g^2}{\sigma_\beta^2}\Big]
+\lambda_{s}\sum_g\big[(\Delta^2\eta_g)^2+(\Delta^2\zeta_g)^2\big]
\end{aligned}
$$

$\eta_g=\ln\alpha_g$ (incidence), $\zeta_g=\ln\beta_g$ (mortality), bands `r paste(I$cal$meta$bands, collapse = ", ")`. Weights $w$ = `r paste(I$cal$layer1$optimizer_diagnostics$weights, collapse = ", ")`; $\omega$ inverse-variance from GBD intervals (`r if (isTRUE(I$cal$layer1$optimizer_diagnostics$used_iv_weights)) "used" else "not used"`). $\sigma_\alpha$ = `r I$cal$layer1$optimizer_diagnostics$priors[["sigma_alpha"]]`, $\sigma_\beta$ = `r I$cal$layer1$optimizer_diagnostics$priors[["sigma_beta"]]`. `r I$cal$layer1$optimizer_diagnostics$optimizer` L-BFGS-B, `r I$cal$layer1$optimizer_diagnostics$n_starts` random starts plus baseline. Only $\alpha$ is used, as Layer-2 start values.

## Layer 2 minimises weighted log errors on masked cells plus mortality and structural priors

$$
\begin{aligned}
L_2={}&w_P\bar\ell_P+w_D\bar\ell_D+w_I\bar\ell_I+w_S\bar\ell_S+\lambda_m\frac{(\ln m_D-\ln m_D^0)^2}{\sigma_m^2}\\
&+\lambda_s\Big[\sum_k\frac{(\mathrm{logit}\,p_k-\mathrm{logit}\,p^0_k)^2}{\sigma_p^2}+\sum_{b,s}\frac{(\ln\alpha_{bs})^2}{\sigma_\alpha^2}+R_{\mathrm{age}}\Big]+\lambda_\Delta\sum_{s,b}(\Delta^2\ln\alpha_{bs})^2
\end{aligned}
$$

$\bar\ell_X$: weighted mean of $[\ln(X^{\mathrm{mod}}+\varepsilon)-\ln(X^{\mathrm{tgt}}+\varepsilon)]^2$ over unmasked cells, both sexes pooled. $w_P,w_D,w_I,w_S$ = `r paste(fmt_f(I$oc$weights, 1), collapse = ", ")`; $\lambda_m$ = `r fmt_f(I$oc$lambda_prior_mortality, 2)`, $\lambda_s$ = `r fmt_f(I$oc$lambda_prior_structural, 2)`, $\lambda_\Delta$ = `r I$sc$priors$lambda_smooth_alpha`; $\sigma_m$ = `r I$sc$priors$sigma_mort`, $\sigma_p$ = `r I$sc$priors$sigma_trans`, $\sigma_\alpha$ = `r I$sc$priors$sigma_alpha`. Settings as saved for Indonesia; Uganda's are identical (checked in the next slide).

## Scored cells are `r if (FLOOR > 0) "adult deaths" else "all-age deaths"` and all-age prevalence in `r I$oc$match_from`–`r CY`; the rest are validation

```{r tab-cells}
cells <- function(r) { f <- copy(r$fl)
  f[, status := fcase(held_out, "Held-out year", in_loss, "Scored",
                      is.na(target_used), "Missing (masked)",
                      measure == "Incidence" & r$oc$weights[["W_INC"]] == 0, "Validation only",
                      measure == "Deaths" & glo < r$floor, paste0("Under ", r$floor, " (masked)"),
                      default = "Below count threshold")]
  dcast(f[, .N, by = .(measure, status)], status ~ measure, value.var = "N", fill = 0) }
ci <- cells(I); cu <- cells(U)
cm <- merge(ci, cu, by = "status", all = TRUE, suffixes = c(".i", ".u"))
for (j in names(cm)[-1]) set(cm, which(is.na(cm[[j]])), j, 0L)
cm_tab <- cm[, .(Status = status, Prev.i = Prevalence.i, Deaths.i = Deaths.i, Inc.i = Incidence.i,
                 Prev.u = Prevalence.u, Deaths.u = Deaths.u, Inc.u = Incidence.u)]
names(cm_tab) <- c("Cell status", "Prev.", "Deaths", "Incid.", "Prev.", "Deaths", "Incid.")
same_settings <- isTRUE(all.equal(I$oc[c("weights", "lambda_prior_mortality", "lambda_prior_structural", "match_from", "death_target_age_min")],
                                  U$oc[c("weights", "lambda_prior_mortality", "lambda_prior_structural", "match_from", "death_target_age_min")])) &&
  isTRUE(all.equal(I$sc$priors[c("sigma_mort", "sigma_trans", "sigma_alpha", "lambda_smooth_alpha")],
                   U$sc$priors[c("sigma_mort", "sigma_trans", "sigma_alpha", "lambda_smooth_alpha")]))
kb(cm_tab, "lrrrrrr", font = 9) |> add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Indonesia" = 3, "Uganda" = 3))
```

\srcline Age-group $\times$ sex $\times$ year cells, `r I$cal$meta$calib_year_start`–`r CY`. Objective settings `r if (same_settings) "are identical in the two countries" else "differ between the countries"`. Masking as recorded: `r gsub("_", "\\\\_", gsub("<", "$<$", I$oc$masking))`.

## Calibrated transitions, stage-D mortality and adult multipliers, with priors and bounds

```{r tab-params}
prow <- function(r, p, d = 4) { x <- r$ptab[parameter == p]
  if (!nrow(x)) return(c("fixed", fmt_f(r$tr[[p]], d)))
  sc <- function(v) if (grepl("^p_", p)) plogis(v) else exp(v)
  b <- if (isTRUE(x$at_lower) || isTRUE(x$at_upper)) "\\prov{\\textbf{" else ""
  c(paste0(fmt_f(x$prior_center, d), " [", fmt_f(sc(x$lower), 3), ", ", fmt_f(sc(x$upper), 3), "]"),
    paste0(b, fmt_f(x$value, d), if (nzchar(b)) "}}" else "")) }
pars <- c(tp_rows, "log_mD", "log_adult_prog_mult", "log_adult_remission_mult")
plab <- c(unname(tp_lab[tp_rows]), "Stage-D mortality", "Adult progression multiplier", "Adult remission multiplier")
pi_ <- t(vapply(pars, function(p) prow(I, p), c("", ""))); pu_ <- t(vapply(pars, function(p) prow(U, p), c("", "")))
par_tab <- data.frame(Parameter = plab, pi = pi_[, 1], vi = pi_[, 2], pu = pu_[, 1], vu = pu_[, 2])
names(par_tab) <- c("Annual probability or multiplier", "Prior [bounds]", "Fitted", "Prior [bounds]", "Fitted")
kb(par_tab, "lrrrr", font = 8) |> add_header_above(c(" " = 1, "Indonesia" = 2, "Uganda" = 2))
```

\srcline Transitions apply below age `r I$bp$age_structure$adult_age_cutoff`; multipliers act on adult hazards, $p_{\mathrm{adult}}=1-(1-p)^{\kappa}$. Amber bold: at a bound. `r if (D_ONLY) "Stage A--C RHD mortality is exactly zero; residual multiplier fixed at 1." else ""`

## The burn-in converges and the bridge carries the calibrated state to `r Y0`

```{r tab-init}
ini <- function(r) { b <- as.data.table(r$sc$burnin_check); br <- as.data.table(r$sc$bridge_reconciliation)
  last_gbd <- br[!grepl("seed", measure) & !is.na(gbd_number)]
  ly <- max(last_gbd$year); seed <- br[grepl("seed", measure)]
  c(paste(r$sc$priors$burn_years, "/", 2L * r$sc$priors$burn_years), fmt_e(max(b$rel_diff_2x)),
    fmt_f(last_gbd[measure == "Prevalence" & year == ly, ratio_model_over_rate_x_wpp]),
    fmt_f(last_gbd[measure == "Deaths" & year == ly, ratio_model_over_rate_x_wpp]),
    if (nrow(seed)) fmt_f(seed$ratio_model_over_rate_x_wpp) else "n/a") }
lyr <- max(as.data.table(I$sc$bridge_reconciliation)[!is.na(gbd_number), year])
in_tab <- data.frame(q = c("Burn-in cycles / doubled check", "Largest stage change, doubled burn-in",
                           paste0("Bridge prevalence / GBD, ", lyr), paste0("Bridge RHD deaths / GBD, ", lyr),
                           paste0("Seed entering ", Y0, " / legacy GBD-rate seed")),
                     i = ini(I), u = ini(U))
names(in_tab) <- c("", "Indonesia", "Uganda")
kb(in_tab, "lrr", widths = c("7cm", "2.6cm", "2.6cm"))
```
